params.why: the highest common factor of the two coefficients must be exactly c, and the cubes must not both be plain x^3 and y^3 (that is the basic family)

solution: The largest number that divides both ${=A}$ and ${=B}$ is ${=c}$, so take out the common factor ${=c}$ first: ${=A}x^{3} {=op} {=B}y^{3} = {=c}({=d3c}x^{3} {=op} {=e3c}y^{3})$
Write each term in the bracket as a cube: ${=d3c}x^{3} = ({=dc}x)^{3}$ and ${=e3c}y^{3} = ({=ec}y)^{3}$. The bracket is a {=kind} of two cubes with cube roots ${=dc}x$ and ${=ec}y$.

Use $a^{3} {=op} b^{3} = (a {=op} b)(a^{2} {=op2} ab + b^{2})$ with the cube roots in place of $a$ and $b$: ${=d3c}x^{3} {=op} {=e3c}y^{3} = ({=dc}x {=op} {=ec}y)[({=dc}x)^{2} {=op2} ({=dc}x)({=ec}y) + ({=ec}y)^{2}]$
Simplify the second bracket and keep the common factor in front: ${=A}x^{3} {=op} {=B}y^{3} = {=c}({=dc}x {=op} {=ec}y)({=d2c}x^{2} {=op2} {=dec}xy + {=e2c}y^{2})$

proposed_misconceptions.label: Drops the common factor
proposed_misconceptions.description: Takes the common factor out and factorises the bracket, but leaves the factor out of the final answer.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Wrong cube root of a coefficient
proposed_misconceptions.description: Writes the cube coefficient itself, or its square root, as the term in the first bracket, e.g. 64m^3 gives (64m + f) or (8m + f) instead of (4m + f).

proposed_misconceptions.label: Coefficient not squared in the trinomial
proposed_misconceptions.description: Squares only the letter when building the trinomial, so (2x)^2 becomes 2x^2 instead of 4x^2, and the middle term and last term are built from the unsquared coefficients.

notes: Models ex1-9-19 (128m^3+2f^3 = 2(4m+f)(16m^2-4mf+f^2)) and ex1-9-7. d and e are the cube roots of the two coefficients left after the common factor c is taken out; they are coprime so the HCF of the two printed coefficients is exactly c (a solver cannot legitimately take out more). d=e=1 is excluded because that is the basic family. When d or e is 1 the template drops the 1 (x^3, not 1x^3). c is never 1 or 8. Instances: 4 values of c, 10 coprime pairs, sum or difference = 80. Largest coefficient 5*64 = 320.
